home.intro: **Good enough is not good enough.** I test my own systems against themselves and keep improving them, so the work rarely sits in a resting state. All of it runs on design systems and a custom AI harness tuned to my workflow, built over the last four months — it started as a simple loop and became the design and production system everything here goes through. Everything below runs; nothing here is a mockup. Running is not the same as finished, and the games are where that shows.

stage_v2._: CR-32, Site card item 43. Read by scripts/build_project_sizes.py (and by the stage, chunk 2). Named stage_v2 and not stage because home.stage above is CR-25's list of three start-here panels, which composition a still renders; the stage retires that list. repos: a PRIVATE map, slug -> the project's folder relative to the projects root, read only by the size generator and never written to a page. The folder names are public in this file: they are not links and every slug is already public (the master keeps them). It exists because a registry `repo` becomes a public link and several of these repositories are private. The generator uses the map first, then the registry repo URL against each origin; a slug in neither stays could_not_look. Each entry was matched by an exact folder or origin name with one candidate; design-first is the canonical Node kit (tools/design-first is the stale PowerShell reference copy). tiers: a project with fewer commits than small_below is small, one with large_from or more is large, the rest are medium; a project the measure could not see is small and never guessed up. overrides: { slug: { tier, reason } } - the tier is small, medium or large and the reason is one written line; a missing reason is refused. sizes.scan_depth is how many folders below the projects root a repository may sit; sizes.skip_dirs are folder names, and sizes.skip_prefixes folder-name prefixes, that the scan never enters (an underscore folder holds scratch unzips, backups and the archive). Thresholds 5 and 30 (CR-32): chosen on 2026-10-21 from the 28 measured running projects so that the tiers split them roughly in thirds (11 small, 8 medium, 9 large); recompute them when the distribution has moved.

index._: CR-25. The typographic index. A project is a row when its status is in statuses. cats are registry category slugs. door is a screen id, or empty: the group heading links to that screen.
